verdicts.evidence: Seeded a failure whose log was a realistic webpack run and loaded the screen. What renders is an error Banner reading "The publish did not finish: the extension did not build (verifier 08-failed)" (the real recorded message) and then an SCard titled "The line that looks like the problem" whose body is the raw log line "ERROR in ./pages/NodeHealth.vue", followed by the hint "Picked out of the log by pattern, not by understanding it - the assistant does not yet read a build log and explain it. Treat this as a pointer to where to look." The heuristic is firstError() in build-failed.vue: the first log line matching /^(ERROR|error|Module not found|SyntaxError|TypeError|Failed to)/, then any line containing "error". Seeded a second failure whose log contains no error-looking line ("INFO Building for production... / Done in 12.3s.") and the card disappeared entirely, leaving only the banner and the log. The wording is honest about the gap, and the page comment says the same thing.
verdicts.defect: There is no plain-language explanation. The design promises an alert icon, a plain-language headline ("The page renders on a blank screen"), a sub-line separating build success from the real fault ("Build succeeded - the route has no parent chrome") and a paragraph explaining the cause. The product substitutes a raw log line picked by regex, and when the regex matches nothing the screen explains nothing at all. The "explained" half of the screen title is not delivered. The honest labelling is the right call given that, and should be kept if this is ever implemented properly.

verdicts.evidence: The real recorded log renders in full, always expanded, in a panel headed "Build log": the seven lines I seeded came back byte for byte in .failed__log, including my marker line. verdicts.evidence: grep -rF "Undo my request" over pkg/barn returns nothing. Nothing in the codebase reverts a whole assistant turn: extensions.ts has undoLastChange (one file, the most recently modified changed one), restoreSnapshot (the whole tree, back to a named point) and discard-all in review.vue. There is no per-turn record to revert, because nothing records which files a given request touched.
verdicts.defect: The design deliberately makes "Undo last change" (masthead, one edit) and "Undo my request" (conversation, the whole turn that caused the failure) different scopes. The product distinguishes neither: it has one file-scoped undo and one tree-scoped restore, and no notion of a turn at all. Implementing the request scope needs authoring provenance to be captured per turn, which is the same data screen 12 needs for per-hunk prompt provenance.

verdicts.evidence: grep -rF "Roll back" over pkg/barn returns nothing, and no masthead roll-back button exists on this route: Enumerated every control the route renders: with a failure seeded, the whole of `.failed` contains exactly four interactive elements (button[aria-label=Back], "Fix it with the assistant", "See what changed (pages/NodeHealth.vue)", "Try the publish again") plus an error banner, the "line that looks like the problem" card and the Build log panel. I did verify the capability behind it, on screen 03 and against a snapshot of my own. In the pod I wrote /app/pkg/base/verify-08-failed.txt containing "A", then used EditorMasthead's Snapshots menu (data-testid barn-snapshots-menu) to take a snapshot named "verify-08-failed rollback A"; the toast read '"verify-08-failed rollback A" holds the working tree as it is now (d5ec269)' and git for-each-ref in the pod showed the new tag barn-snap/1787448855262. I changed the file to "B", reopened the menu, chose my own snapshot (never the pre-existing "probe point A"), confirmed the dialog and clicked "Restore the files". The file was "A" again, and md5sums of every other changed file in the tree (BRIEF.md, CLAUDE.md, verify-04-review-new.txt, verify-04-review-staged.txt) were unchanged before and after, so no other verifier's work moved. I then deleted my file and my tag and put the index back as I found it.
verdicts.defect: The screen the design puts this button on has no way back on it at all. The guarantee the caption calls out ("guaranteed way back") is real underneath (snapshots are tagged commit objects built from a scratch index, so untracked files are included, and restoreSnapshot is a real git checkout), but it is reachable only from a menu on the editor screen, and only if somebody thought to take a snapshot first. Nothing snapshots automatically per build, so on this screen after a failed build there may be no snapshot to roll back to.

verdicts.defect: The query parameter is dead. Nothing in editor.vue reads $route.query.publish (it reads only $route.query.tab), so "Try the publish again" does not retry the publish: it drops you on the workspace, having thrown away the failure record and its log on the way. Either the editor should act on ?publish=local, or the button should be labelled for what it does. Separately, the design draws Publish itself enabled in this state and there is no Publish on this screen at all, so the "one hard gate" question this state raises is not answered here.
